doc.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Variety of gigs, including Motown horn sections
summary: He plays private parties and events, and in Detroit played local horn sections behind the Temptations, Four Tops and Martha Reeves.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Do you augment these kind of gigs with anything like pit bands or playing theater shows, that kind of thing?

Not so much theater and pit bands. I do live in New York so you’d think maybe I was doing Broadway. But that’s kind of a very specific kind of playing that I’m not as interested in and not really as cut out for that, although I read and everything, that’s not the problem, it’s just that I don’t think I would enjoy it mostly. But I have always done different kinds of gigs and I’ll do private parties, which could mean weddings or anniversary parties, or things like that, dances, or oh, any number of things, all kinds of little industrial events, sometimes they’ll hire a band to play. And you know all different kinds of things like that. And I have played like shows behind singers in groups. Back when I lived in Detroit I used to play in bands. The Motown groups would come through town and use local horn sections. They’d have their rhythm sections that they’d travel with and they’d hire local horn players, and that was fun. I got to play with, you know, the Temptations and the Four Tops, and Martha Reeves, and the OJ’s, and groups like that. And that was fun. They were always very professional, nice guys and I think they really appreciated the Detroit horn sections because most of us had grown up with that music and we knew how it was supposed to go. They didn’t have to go through and rehearse too long with us, you know.
Looks good on your resume, too, huh?

Yeah. I played with the Temptations — you know. Except the people at a party like this, an event like this, probably wouldn’t be as excited about that as the younger folks. They’d say what is this, rock & roll? Yeah I’ve always done kind of a variety of gigs. That’s one of the things I like about being a musician is that I’m not always playing with the same people and at the same kind of place. I kind of like the challenge of doing a variety of kinds of music.
